children: Premier Energies is expanding beyond solar manufacturing as rising renewable capacity and grid-balancing needs accelerate demand for battery energy storage in India

Premier Energies is targeting June 2027 for commissioning the first 6 GWh phase of its planned 12 GWh battery energy storage system manufacturing business in Telangana, as the solar manufacturer moves to broaden its clean-energy portfolio amid growing demand for firm and dispatchable renewable power. The company is developing the battery storage business through a joint venture with Germany-based RCT Solutions.

The initial phase will have a capacity of 6 GWh, with the overall facility planned at 12 GWh. The storage business is expected to cater to commercial, industrial and utility-scale customers, while also creating an export opportunity. The move comes as India's renewable energy expansion increasingly shifts the focus from generation capacity to storage, transmission and grid flexibility. India had crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity by July 2026, while the government has set a target of 500 GW by 2030.

As solar and wind capacity expands, battery storage is becoming increasingly important to manage intermittent generation and match electricity supply with demand during peak periods. Industry experts say the growing requirement for round-the-clock renewable power, peak-demand management and grid balancing is creating a structural market for BESS manufacturing in India. They add that domestic production could also reduce supply-chain exposure as storage deployment scales. Government policy is also supporting the sector through viability-gap funding, domestic-content requirements and incentives for co-located storage.

Premier Energies has previously highlighted government support for 43.8 GWh of battery storage capacity, including a capital subsidy of Rs 91.6 billion. The company is therefore entering a market where policy support and rising renewable penetration are converging with increasing requirements for flexible power infrastructure.

Premier Energies is simultaneously strengthening its position across the solar manufacturing value chain. On September 21, the company commissioned a 7 GW N-type TOPCon G12R solar-cell manufacturing facility at Naidupeta in Andhra Pradesh.

The facility, developed at an investment of around Rs 32.93 billion, takes the company's total solar-cell manufacturing capacity to 10.6 GW. Premier Energies is also developing 10 GW of ingot and wafer manufacturing capacity at Naidupeta as part of its backwards-integration strategy.

The company's expansion into batteries, solar manufacturing and transformers reflects the broader industry trend towards integrated clean-energy platforms. For manufacturers, the shift offers an opportunity to participate in multiple segments of India's energy transition rather than relying solely on solar-module and cell demand. With renewable additions continuing to rise, the economics of India's power transition are increasingly dependent not only on adding generation capacity but also on building the storage and grid infrastructure required to use that electricity efficiently.
